title: The Holy Order - Cathedral, Vigil and Judgement - Sacred Fantasy RPG Game Music Pack - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track sacred fantasy score: choir in every track, every loop closes on an Amen cadence. MIDI + OGG.
description:
The Holy Order is a 44 track score for the holy order in a fantasy game, from the morning bell to the ascension: the cathedral city and the city at vespers, the pilgrims' market and hospice, the scriptorium and the cloister garden, the pilgrim road, the wayside shrines and the abbey woods, the mountain monastery, the great nave, the choir stalls, the bell tower, the lady chapel, the founders' crypt and the night office, the knights of the order, the chapter house and the oath, the inquisition, the heretic's cell, the trial and the forbidden archive, a battle set and three bosses, a requiem, a miracle, the ascension and an ending, and the cues a game fires all day.

The Amen at every loop. Every one of the 38 full pieces closes its loop on a plagal cadence, the Amen: the chord on the fourth degree, then the tonic, as the last thing heard before the music wraps. Checked on the shipped MIDI, track by track: over the last two chord spans before the loop point the pad plays exactly the fourth degree triad and then exactly the tonic triad, and the bass starts each one on its root. 38 of 38. The same reading over the other 31 albums in this studio's catalogue, 1056 full pieces, finds 148 that happen to end that way and no album that does it on every piece.

The intonation. In chant the cantor sings the opening phrase alone and the choir answers. Every full piece here opens the same way: the lead states the album's theme, Introit, at its written length, adds a short rising answer and holds, and no other part sounds until it has finished. The harmony and the bass enter with the loop. The opening plays once and the loop starts after it, so a game hears the lone line when the music starts and the full texture every time it loops. 38 of 38, checked on the MIDI.

A choir in every track. Choir aahs or voice oohs plays in all 44 tracks: as the held harmony under the tune on 39, and singing the tune itself on 5, over a reed organ, strings or a pad. The organ here is the General MIDI reed organ, a harmonium, not a pipe organ.

One theme, every track. Every one of the 44 tracks states Introit in its own shape, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI. 5 more themes sit beside it: one for the high places and the great days, one that is Introit turned upside down for the night offices and the dead, one for the inquisition and the fights, one for the road and the city, and one for the bells.

What is in it. 38 full pieces and 6 short cues, 58:50 of music, 10 in Ionian, 8 in Dorian, 8 in Mixolydian, 8 in Aeolian, 5 in Phrygian, 3 in harmonic minor and 2 in Lydian, 35 tracks in 4/4 and 9 in 3/4. Every note on the record is inside its track's declared mode. The Order: The Holy Order, The Matins Bell, The Cathedral City, The City at Vespers, The Pilgrims' Market, The Pilgrims' Hospice, The Scriptorium and The Cloister Garden. The road: The Pilgrim Road, The Wayside Shrines, The Fields at Compline, The Abbey Woods, The Hermit's Wood and The Mountain Monastery. The cathedral: The Great Nave, The Choir Stalls, The Bell Tower, The Lady Chapel, The Founders' Crypt, The Night Office and Before the Altar. The knights and the inquisition: The Knights of the Order, The Chapter House, The Oath of Investiture, The Inquisition, The Heretic's Cell, The Trial and The Forbidden Archive. The fights: Steel and Scripture, The Zealots, The Last Sanctuary, The Grand Inquisitor, The Fallen Paladin and The False Saint. The ascension: Requiem, The Miracle, The Ascension and The Order Endures. Cues: Thanks Be, Ashes to Ashes, Blessed, A Relic Found, Sanctuary and The Bells Ring Out.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 38 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read. 44 editable .mid sources. A Readme with per engine import notes, the proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

One family of 6 themes. Introit, Gloria, Vigil, Judgement, Pilgrim and The Peal. Introit rises a step and a third and falls back by step, the way a chant opening does; Gloria opens with a leap up a fourth for the high places; Vigil is Introit turned upside down and slowed; Judgement zigzags, a step down and a third up, twice; Pilgrim opens on a rising third for the road; The Peal falls by step and leaps back a fifth, for the bells. 2632 statements and fragments of those themes across the album, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI.

Gate results. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, and the reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Three full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: The Holy Order, the title theme, The Great Nave, a sung lead over the reed organ, and The Grand Inquisitor, the boss. Listen to how each one opens, and to the last two chords before it loops.

An honest note. The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont, so the choirs, organ, bells and brass are the General MIDI sounds of those names; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace them. The order, its city and its saints are invented. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.body:
The Holy Order is a 44 track score for the holy order in a fantasy game: the cathedral city, the pilgrim road, the scriptorium and the cloister, the great nave, the bell tower and the crypt, the knights of the order, the inquisition and the trial, a battle set and three bosses, a requiem, a miracle and the ascension, and the cues a game fires all day. It is live now, with three full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. Every one of the 38 full pieces closes its loop on a plagal cadence, the Amen: the chord on the fourth degree and then the tonic, the last thing heard before the music wraps. Checked in the shipped MIDI: 38 of 38, the pad exactly those two triads and the bass on each root. Across the other 31 albums in our catalogue, 148 of 1056 full pieces happen to end that way and none does it on every piece. Every full piece also opens with the theme played by one voice alone, the way a cantor intones a chant, and a choir sings in all 44 tracks.

How it was checked. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks (The Holy Order, The Great Nave and The Grand Inquisitor) are for.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render; load the MIDI into your own instruments to replace the sounds. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
